summary: Pramod Chandra worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University (~1952–1954) and held posts at the University of Chicago (~1964–1980) and Harvard University (~1980–2003) as Professor, where he taught Marylin Martin Rhie.

Prapod Assavavirulhakarn specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Chulalongkorn University (attested 1998) and Ryukoku University (attested 2014) as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師).
Prasarn Lao-areun works in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He studied under teacher Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).
Pratap Kumar Penumala works in religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.
Pratapaditya Pal works in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1970–1995, attested 2007) and the Art Institute of Chicago (1995).

Prayoon Mererk works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985, studying under doctoral supervisors Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He earned degrees from the University of Oslo and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, later holding posts at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University (~1993–2014).

Projit Bihari Mukharji works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and SOAS, later holding posts at Newcastle University, McMaster University, the University of Pennsylvania (~2011–2022), and Ashoka University (~2022).

Pulinbihari Chakravarti worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under teachers Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee, and served as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society (attested 1951).

Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and earned a PhD from La Trobe University, later holding posts at Deakin, Melbourne, Columbia, Stony Brook, and UC Berkeley.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).
Pál Miklós was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1946–1950) and Peking University (~1950–1954), and later taught Lilla Russell-Smith.

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College under Alexis Sanderson, and held posts as a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington, where she was supervised by Collett Cox and taught by Rupert Gethin, among others.

Qiang Ning works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under doctoral supervisors Wu Hung and Irene Winter, and held posts at the Dunhuang Academy, San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan.

Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Kang Youwei (~1890–1898) and at National Tsing Hua University, later holding a post at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929).

Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg, and served as a Professor at Peking University (~1987–2022), where she taught Shaoyong Ye.

Qingying Chen worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Qinghai Normal University, Qinghai University for Nationalities, and Minzu University of China, later holding posts at Southwest Minzu University, Minzu University, and China Tibetology Research Center (~1988–2012).
Qingzhi Zhu specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and The Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).

Qinni Liu works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009), studying under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin and committee members D.-D. Huang and Cheng-I Weng.
